objectives.description: Introduction to Painting: meaning of pictorial and decorative painting; differences between pictorial and decorative paintings; tools and equipment; elements and principles of design; functions of pictorial and decorative painting.

Colour Theory: meaning of colour; classes of colour (primary, secondary and tertiary); properties of colour (hues, tones and intensity); colour schemes (analogous, complementary and monochromes); improvisation of colours from local sources.
Techniques in Pictorial Painting: dry painting, wet painting, glazing, impasto, fresco, tempera.
Techniques in Decorative Painting: flat painting, rag rolling, scumbling or combing, spraying, mural, mosaic.
Types and Functions of Pictorial Painting: still life painting, nature painting, figure/life painting; differences between observatory and imaginative painting compositions; functions.

Types and Functions of Decorative Painting: body decoration (meaning, differences between traditional and modern, motifs and designs, materials, functions); wall decoration (meaning, differences between traditional and modern, motifs/patterns/designs, materials, functions).
Perspective: meaning; types; importance of perspective in pictorial painting composition.
Prospects in Painting: the socio-economic value of pictorial and decorative painting; careers in pictorial and decorative painting.

Costing/Marketing of Paintings: costing based on location and size, materials/equipment, time invested, quantity and quality; exhibition of paintings (planning/processes, funding); marketing (pricing, negotiation, communication/advertising, outlets, selling).
